prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Full SCENE STATE SHEET for a physical Mars expedition game. Match the supplied realistic painterly cream-and-teal machinery, ochre landscape, restrained cobalt science equipment, mustard rover fittings. Locally made parts are simple cut straight steel and bolted joints, never elaborate molded industrial machinery. Factory precision parts are imported. No people, text, numerals, labels, captions, borders, arrows, diagrams or UI. Each panel repeats EXACTLY the same camera, framing, object positions, light, room/landscape and perspective, changing ONLY the specified state. Every recurring object is the same actual object. Frame the full installation in the upper two thirds; lower third is quiet natural floor or ground for the movable inventory. No loose decorative objects. Whole scenes will be cropped into registered fixed targets; keep independent working regions clearly separated. Square panels, not portrait strips.
Layout: 3 columns by 1 rows of equal SQUARE scenes. Reading order left to right then next row. Use the FINAL panel of reference 1 as the starting construction: same cream pressure room, three bolted growing zones (deep left potato bay, narrow back soybean row, shallow right lettuce shelf), one shared reservoir and return air gap. Add a compact freshwater wall outlet on the far left wall just ahead of the left bed; a small fold-down wash tray directly underneath makes ONE water/wash service point. Keep a clear exposed hose route along the wall and floor from this outlet to the existing common reservoir, away from the growing surfaces.
STATE 1: All three beds are empty lined trays. Water outlet and wash tray exist. No fresh-water feed hose yet.
STATE 2: All three trays now contain clean light-brown porous granular growing medium. No seeds or plants. The hose route is still empty.
STATE 3: Same medium-filled beds. A slim blue-coupled supply hose now joins the freshwater wall outlet to the EXISTING shared reservoir. Keep the return air gap above the reservoir. Do not add a second pump, tank or bed.
